theme: Anxiety and faith; feeling rejected or misunderstood; trusting God without having all the answers; finding peace through prayer; surrendering the need to understand and control; God's peace during fear, uncertainty, and difficult circumstances.
prayer: Lord, sometimes my mind will not stop trying to understand, anticipate, protect, and prepare. When I feel rejected, frightened, misunderstood, or uncertain, remind me that I do not have to solve everything before bringing it to You. Take what I cannot understand and what I cannot control. Guard my heart and mind when I am tired of standing guard myself. Let Your peace meet me before the answers do. Amen.
body:
I woke from a nightmare this morning with that feeling. Everyone was against me.
No one actually said it directly. That almost made it worse. I had to figure it out from what people were doing, what they weren't saying, the looks, the conversations happening somewhere else. I found myself calculating everything. What does that mean? Are they talking about me? Am I supposed to leave? How do I leave without making this worse?
At one point, I overheard that a police officer was being called to escort someone out. I assumed it was me. So I quietly began gathering my things while everyone was somewhere else. I didn't need to be escorted. I understood. I would leave. Even in a dream, I was trying to make my rejection easier for everyone else.
There was one person I trusted, and I deliberately kept her out of it. I didn't tell her what was happening. Somehow I wanted to protect the one relationship that still felt safe. Yet even with her, there had been a moment when I felt left out. Then I tried to leave and realized I had only one shoe on. I had to go back for the other one, afraid someone would see me.
There were other strange pieces. A flooding bathroom. A small tower of quarters. People doing something that seemed more enjoyable while I was left doing what was expected. My lead PA appeared and, instead of confronting me, she was crying. I don't know why. I don't know what most of it means. But I know what it felt like: rejected, watched, uncertain, and constantly trying to figure out what I needed to do next.
Then I read today's second reading: “Have no anxiety at all.”
I almost have to stop there. How do you tell an anxious person not to be anxious? How do you tell a mind that has spent the night calculating every possible threat to simply stop?
But Paul doesn't stop there either. “Have no anxiety at all, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, make your requests known to God.”
Maybe the instruction isn't simply stop being anxious. Maybe it is give the anxiety somewhere to go.
Tell God. Tell Him the thing that makes no sense, what someone did, what you are afraid will happen, the conversation you keep replaying. Tell Him you feel rejected. Tell Him you're angry. Tell Him you're exhausted from trying to determine what everyone else is thinking. Tell Him even when you don't know what to ask Him to do about it.
And then Paul says something I might have passed over if we hadn't just spent these days with Job: “The peace of God that surpasses all understanding will guard your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus.”
Surpasses understanding.
Job spent so much time trying to understand. Why did this happen? What have I done? Why won't God explain Himself? Finally God speaks from the storm, and Job realizes there are things too wonderful for him to understand. He never receives the explanation he demanded. He receives God.
Yesterday Job said, “I had heard of you by word of mouth, but now my eye has seen you.” Today Paul tells us about a peace that doesn't require us to understand everything first. Maybe those belong together.
We spend enormous amounts of energy trying to understand things because understanding feels like protection. If I can figure out why someone behaved that way, I can respond correctly. If I know what they're thinking, I can prepare. If I can anticipate what happens next, maybe I can prevent it. If I explain myself clearly enough, maybe they will understand. If I can just figure everything out, maybe I will finally feel safe.
But sometimes there is nothing more to figure out. Sometimes we don't know what another person thinks. We don't know why something happened. We don't know what will happen next. We don't even know whether the thing we fear is actually happening or whether fear has filled in what we cannot see. And the mind keeps calculating anyway.
Paul offers another place for all of that energy to go: prayer, petition, thanksgiving, God.
Not because prayer guarantees the outcome we want. Paul doesn't say that. He says God's peace will guard our hearts and minds.
I find that word beautiful today. Guard. Maybe because so much anxiety comes from believing that we have to guard ourselves—against rejection, against being misunderstood, against the next thing going wrong. Watch everything. Read every signal. Stay ahead of whatever might happen.
What if, for a moment, we stopped standing guard? Not because nothing difficult can happen. It can. Not because every fear is imaginary. It isn't. But because there is Someone else capable of standing watch.
Yesterday Job discovered the sovereignty of God. Today Paul tells us what can happen when we begin to trust it.
Peace can stand guard where we finally stop trying to.
I still don't know what my dream meant. Maybe it doesn't need to mean anything. I know only that I woke carrying its fear. So today I can bring God exactly that—not after I understand it, not after I stop feeling it, not after I have figured out what to do. Now.
Because maybe the peace that surpasses understanding comes precisely when understanding is something we do not have.
opening: Have you ever felt as though everyone was against you, even when you couldn't quite explain why?
title: Relentless Anxiety
